LESSON: EARLY CIVILISATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 2.2: Early Civilisation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Early Civilisation, part of People and Relationships in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How has early African civilisation influenced the world today?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explore factors that led to the growth of the selected ancient Kingdoms in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Early Civilisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. locate the selected ancient Kingdoms on a map of Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Early Civilisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. assess the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Early Civilisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Early Civilisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explore factors that led to the growth of the selected ancient Kingdoms in Africa,

   Early Civilisation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. locate the selected ancient Kingdoms on a map of Africa,

   Early Civilisation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. assess the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation,

   Early Civilisation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.

   Early Civilisation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on factors that led to the growth of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo,

2. use appropriate digital or print media to find out the location of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo from the map of Africa,

3. watch and critique audio-visual documentary on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation,

4. write an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of the modern world civilisation and present it in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on factors that led to the growth of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo,
2. use appropriate digital or print media to find out the location of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo from the map of Africa,
3. watch and critique audio-visual documentary on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation,
4. write an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of the modern world civilisation and present it in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Early Civilisation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking: learners watch and critique audio-visual documentaries on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern

world civilisation.

Values:
Unity: learners watch and critique audio-visual documentaries on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world

civilisation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem: learners write and present in class an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of modern

world civilisation.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Creative Arts: learners relate the ancient contribution of Ancient to the modern world civilisation, by applying knowledge

drawn from architectural designs, dressing, and artefacts.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. explore factors that led to the growth of the selected ancient Kingdoms in Africa,
2. locate the selected ancient Kingdoms on a map of Africa,
3. assess the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation,
4. appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.

Remember the key question: How has early African civilisation influenced the world today?
